scope: Observed late-time acceleration and inferred cosmological-constant parameters versus microscopic vacuum-energy decomposition and radiative response; no GU cosmology or vacuum-energy calculation is performed.

primary_sources.observable_carrier: Type-Ia-supernova light curves, redshifts and luminosity-distance relations
primary_sources.inference_map: calibrated supernova distances and redshifts -> expansion-history likelihood -> acceleration and cosmological parameters within the declared cosmological model
primary_sources.licensed_claim: The high-redshift supernova sample provides evidence for an accelerating universe under the stated analysis.
primary_sources.ceiling: The supernova data do not measure a microscopic decomposition of vacuum energy or identify a unique stress-energy mechanism.

primary_sources.observable_carrier: forty-two high-redshift Type-Ia-supernova light curves, redshifts and fitted luminosity distances
primary_sources.inference_map: supernova Hubble diagram -> Omega_M and Omega_Lambda likelihood under the declared FLRW families
primary_sources.licensed_claim: The sample favors positive Lambda-like late-time acceleration in the fitted cosmological families.
primary_sources.ceiling: A fitted Omega_Lambda is an effective cosmological parameter, not a direct measurement of bare quantum-field vacuum terms.

primary_sources.observable_carrier: CMB temperature, polarization and lensing spectra, including the acoustic angular scale
primary_sources.inference_map: CMB spectra and likelihood -> base-Lambda-CDM and extension-conditional parameter posteriors
primary_sources.licensed_claim: Planck finds good consistency with base Lambda-CDM and infers its late-time parameters under that model.
primary_sources.ceiling: Model-conditional consistency does not determine a microscopic vacuum-energy owner or prove radiative stability.

primary_sources.observable_carrier: DESI DR2 BAO distance ratios combined with named CMB and supernova likelihoods
primary_sources.inference_map: BAO and companion likelihoods -> flat-Lambda-CDM and time-varying-dark-energy comparisons
primary_sources.licensed_claim: Flat Lambda-CDM describes the BAO results, while named combinations prefer a time-varying extension at dataset-dependent significance.
primary_sources.ceiling: The comparison distinguishes effective expansion histories; it does not observe individual microscopic vacuum contributions.

rejected_inferences: late-time acceleration is observed -> a bare microscopic vacuum energy is measured
the incumbent cosmological-constant naturalness problem -> GU need not reproduce the observed expansion history
a fitted effective Lambda -> radiative response and vacuum-shift stability are established
precise_relocation: Treat supernova, CMB and BAO carriers as constraints on an action-owned expansion and perturbation model. Do not require GU to reproduce an unobserved term-by-term microscopic vacuum decomposition, but do require its selected normalization, units, vacuum-shift response and held-out observables.

ledger_comparison.required_revival_token: native or explicitly external normalized observer functional

corrected_evaluation_packet: derive one action-owned normalized background and perturbation model
state how microscopic vacuum shifts enter or cancel in the selected action and domain
predict the observed supernova, CMB and BAO carriers rather than a bare-vacuum decomposition
separate effective late-time parameters from microscopic naturalness claims
